 ETMarkets.com Bitcoin price today crashes near $59,000: Why Peter Brandt warns of a 75% correction as crypto market slides - how low could BTC USD drop next? Bitcoin price crash : BTC USD price today has fallen below $60,000, wiping out more of its recent gains and leaving investors wondering where the sell off will end. The cryptocurrency hit its lowest level since early July on Friday as losses continued across the market. Adding to the anxiety, veteran trader Peter Brandt has warned that Bitcoin could suffer a correction of 75%/ more if its previous market cycles offer any indication of what comes next.
 Bitcoin Price Today Has Dropped Along With Ethereum and Altcoins
Bitcoin touched $59,461 at the time of writing and has been hovering around $60,000 on Friday. It has lost nearly 8.5% over the past week and is now about 51% below its October 2025 all-time high of $126,198.
The slide has dragged other cryptocurrencies lower. Ethereum has fallen nearly 6%, Solana has lost more than 7%, while Zcash has plunged 16.5% in the past 24 hours. 
 BTC USD Outlook: Peter Brandt Warns of a Possible 75% Bitcoin Crash
Could Bitcoin's latest decline turn into another prolonged bear market as Peter Brandt has raised that possibility by pointing to the scale of corrections seen after previous bull-market peaks.
In a social media post on X, Brandt noted, "Every bull market phase in BTC's history has ended with at least a 75% correction of the previous parabolic bull trend," and questioned, "Could this be what's happening in Bitcoin?"

 According to CoinPaper's analysis, Bitcoin fell approximately 84% after its 2017 peak and around 77% during the 2021-2022 downturn.
 So a 75% fall from Bitcoin's October 2025 record of approximately $126,198 would take the price to around $31,550. From Friday's level of roughly $61,900, that would mean another decline of nearly 49%.

Bitcoin is also facing pressure from investors withdrawing money from exchange-traded funds.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $582.3 million in net outflows on November 19. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for around $541.1 million. Total November withdrawals have approached $3.47 billion, as per Farside Investors data cited by CoinPaper.

 Why Is Bitcoin Price USD Falling: Fed Rate Hike and Geopolitical Fears
The sell-off is unfolding against a difficult economic and geopolitical backdrop.
FXStreet reported that the pressure on Bitcoin is risk aversion following the Binance hack, persistent US inflation and tensions in the Middle East. Expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike in December have added to the uncertainty.
Derivatives traders are pricing in 95% odds of a 25-basis-point increase, which would take the federal funds target range to 4.00%-4.25%.
Meanwhile concerns about possible renewed US and Israeli attacks on Iran, stalled Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations and elevated oil prices have added to market anxiety.

 Bitcoin Price Prediction: Will BTC USD Drop to $57,800 Next
Bitcoin's technical picture has deteriorated sharply. The cryptocurrency is trading below its 50-day, 100-day and 200-day exponential moving averages, which are clustered between approximately $74,600 and $75,400.
Its Relative Strength Index (RSI) has fallen to 18, while the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains negative, according to FXStreet.
The yearly low of $57,800 is the next important downside level and CoinPaper has also identified $58,500 and $53,700 as potential support levels.
A recovery above $65,000 could signal an improvement in short term momentum. And move above $70,000 would mark a stronger recovery after the latest losses.
